data.description:
## Context / Problem
`dispatch_apply_phases._call_with_retry` (`:76-148`, 4 attempts) wraps transport calls that already retry — `acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry` (3 attempts), `acli_subprocess._run_acli` (3), DC `_with_connection_retry` — and, on the coordinator route, sits under `retry_budget` replay: up to 12 PUT attempts per plan step (ADR 0103 S3 retires it). After `reroute_ordered_create_plans` (`batch_dispatch.py:524-599`) and `reroute_migrated_plans` (`:742-791`), every planned outbound mutation is already coordinator-routed (plans group by `Mutation.target`, so a mixed create/non-create plan cannot occur); the legacy `_apply_batch` loop only runs for callers passing `ticket_plans=None` (tests). Yet the handlers the coordinator dispatches into still call `_call_with_retry`: update (`dispatch_one.py:661` `update_issue`, `:567` `set_parent`, `:754,756` labels), create (`dispatch_one.py:243` label; `create_route.py:272-274,332,339`), links (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:543,677`), typed leaves (`apply_outbound.py:234,256,281`; `apply_inbound.py:206`; `apply_inbound_events.py:268-269`). Cites are on origin/main 083620b0 (engine paths are under `src/rebar/reconciler/` after the package move).

## Approach
1. Replace every `_call_with_retry(fn, *a, **k)` with `fn(*a, **k)`: single attempt at the handler layer; the transport owns transient retry, the coordinator owns replay.
2. Delete `_call_with_retry`, its re-exports (`batch_dispatch.py:39,69`, `applier.py:137,291`, `dispatch_one.py:54`), and `create_route.py:272-274` `self._call`; keep `RetryExhaustedError` (raised by `acli_subprocess`); `dispatch_one.py:663` `except RetryExhaustedError` stays (transport still raises it).
3. Make `ticket_plans` required on `applier.apply`'s batch form. `remaining` is provably `[]` in production (all planned mutations are rerouted), so delete `_apply_one`'s loop over `remaining`, keeping `_apply_one` for `reroute_ordered_create_plans`' `_dispatch_with_backstop`.
4. Record the ADR 0103 S3 completion in `docs/release-notes.md` and update the `docs/llm-framework.md` reference.

BREAKING: handler-level retry removed; retry counts are the transport's (3) plus coordinator replay.

## Scope
`src/rebar/reconciler/{dispatch_apply_phases,dispatch_one,create_route,apply_outbound,apply_inbound,apply_inbound_events,batch_dispatch,applier}.py`, `tests/unit/reconciler/{apply,mutate}/` retry tests (`test_applier_retry_test`-style modules assert 3 attempts at the transport, not 4×3), `docs/release-notes.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md`. Out of scope: the transport retry loops (`acli_rest`, `acli_subprocess`, DC `_with_connection_retry`) and `retry_budget`, both unchanged.

## Testing
Happy: `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/mutate tests/unit/reconciler/apply -q`. Edge: a fake transport whose `update_issue` raises `HTTPError(503)` once then succeeds — the handler records a single failure outcome (no handler retry) and the coordinator's budget replays it (assert exactly 2 `update_issue` calls end-to-end via `coordinate_and_fuse`); a `TimeoutError` from `create_issue` yields `CreateSignal(status="timeout")` unchanged; `git grep -n '_call_with_retry' -- src` is empty.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_call_with_retry` absent from `src/` — grep.
- [ ] End-to-end attempt count for a transient 503 on update is transport-retries + coordinator replay only — the unit test above.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0; `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` prints `new=0`.
data.title: Retire _call_with_retry so handlers make a single transport attempt (ADR 0103 S3)
